# 5a.3b crypt-count parity fixture.
#
# Provenance: the counting core is unchanged by 5a.3b. Master's Kotlin
# CryptState is a thin wrapper over this same native OCB2 engine (stats
# buffer -> good/late/lost/resync) with the same 5 s resync rule in
# HumlaUDP. The branch's additions to CryptStateOCB2.cpp are the test-only
# backdate hook and a Stop-time clear() that zeroes key material (control
# thread only, receive already joined, never on the decrypt path), so
# neither touches the counting path below. The tuple is what the
# pre-deletion path reports for this scripted sequence, and the native
# test testReceiveCryptCountsMatchKotlin reproduces it through the same
# core.
#
# Scripted sequence (one sender, one receiver, same key; s1..s6 are the
# sender's 1st..6th encrypted packets):
#   1. deliver s1            -> good=1
#   2. replay s1             -> still good=1 (replay rejected, counters hold)
#   3. deliver s6 (skip s2..s5, 4 lost) -> good=2, lost=4
#   4. deliver s4 late       -> good=3, late=1, lost recovers one (lost=3)
#   5. tampered packet with recent good -> suppressed, no resync, hold
#   6. rekey (new IV)        -> counters reset, next good=1, lost=0, late=0
#
# Expected tuple after step 4 (before tamper/rekey):
good=3
late=1
lost=3
resync=0
